WMT.rationale: Walmart is a structurally sound, wide-moat retailer with dominant U.S. grocery share (~21%), accelerating high-margin digital revenue streams (advertising +37%, membership +17%, marketplace +50% in Q1 FY27), and a proven omnichannel model reaching 90% of U.S. households. However, the near-term picture is mixed: Q1 FY27 EPS of $0.67 came in below the prior two quarters ($0.88 and $0.77), operating cash flow fell sharply QoQ (-47.9%), and fuel costs absorbed ~$175M (~250bps of operating income). The stock has pulled back ~13% from its 52-week high of $135.16 to $117.18, and the P/E has compressed from a peak of ~55x in May 2026 to ~40.5x — now near the low end of its 1-year range (39.0-55.4). This valuation compression creates a modestly more attractive entry vs recent history, but 40x earnings for a ~3-4% operating margin retailer still represents a premium that requires continued execution on the high-margin platform layer. The balance sheet is solid ($100.7B equity, $10.7B cash), and management guided for 3.5-4.5% constant-currency sales growth and 6-8% operating income growth for FY27. The next earnings catalyst is August 20, 2026 (Q2 FY27). No strong near-term re-rating catalyst is visible — the stock sold off post-Q1 despite a top-line beat, suggesting the market is already discounting the positive mix-shift narrative at this multiple. Net: good business, improving mix, but richly valued for its margin profile; mild positive tilt from valuation compression.
